subject.title: fix(cron): allow timeoutSeconds: 0 for no-timeout mode

question: Should the Control UI expose the existing cron `timeoutSeconds: 0` no-timeout sentinel, or keep UI-created agent-turn jobs bounded by the current positive-timeout validation?
rationale: The gateway and cron runtime already accept zero, but this PR would make no-watchdog cron jobs easy to create from the UI, which is an availability policy tradeoff that code inspection alone cannot settle.

options.title: Accept with proof and tests
options.body: Refresh the branch to the current UI files, keep zero as an explicit no-timeout value, reject malformed values, and require real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Keep UI bounded
options.body: Close or redirect this PR if maintainers want no-timeout cron jobs to remain unavailable from the Control UI despite lower-level support.

recommendation.title: Accept with proof and tests
recommendation.body: Refresh the branch to the current UI files, keep zero as an explicit no-timeout value, reject malformed values, and require real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly connected to the Control UI cron edit parity surface and the validation/payload behavior under review.
